entries.title: The First Skiff
entries.text: The oldest skiffs carried mirrors instead of cargo. A keeper turned each mirror toward a light on shore, and the next boat followed its reflection. Nothing crossed the entire ocean alone.

entries.title: A Place to Return
entries.text: Before the lamps, the harbor was a promise made in chalk on a warehouse wall: leave one mooring open for the last boat. The first restoration returns that promise to the water.

entries.title: What a Chart Keeps
entries.text: A new chart does not preserve every vessel. It preserves a route, a measurement, and the reason a keeper trusted them. The fleet can be rebuilt around knowledge that remains.

entries.title: The Nursery Glass
entries.text: Prism nurseries grow slowly enough that their first keepers used weather as a calendar. The glass bends light without deciding where it should go. That is still your work.

entries.title: Small Lights, Large Instruments
entries.text: An observatory can see far and still mistake a nearby rock for open water. Skiffs supply the close observations that make its distance useful. Size is not the same as perspective.

entries.title: The Joined Beam
entries.text: The first connected harbor lamps appeared brighter together than apart. The keepers argued about the mathematics until a child pointed out the new channel between them. The argument and the channel both remained on the chart.

entries.title: The Survey Bell
entries.text: The survey bell rings for a completed record, not for a returning keeper. Notes can wait in a dry drawer. A useful harbor should let its people sleep.

entries.title: A Pattern Without Hurry
entries.text: Constellations were named by observers who returned to the same question many nights in a row. A fast hand was never a requirement. A careful eye was welcome, and another way to point was equally good.

entries.title: The Night Ledger
entries.text: A quartermaster began recording not only arrivals, but absences. An empty chair meant someone trusted the harbor to keep working. The ledger made room for that kind of trust.

entries.title: The Narrow Fleet
entries.text: One winter, the channel could carry only a handful of vessels. The keepers stopped asking which boat was best and began asking which combination could bring everyone home.

entries.title: A Different Tide
entries.text: At the outer reefs, familiar links change their strength. A route learned at home can still be useful, but it cannot be copied without looking. The sea rewards attention to what has changed.

entries.title: Instructions for Morning
entries.text: The oldest automatic plan was a note pinned beside a lamp: if the tide reaches this mark, move the mirror. The note worked because someone had made the condition precise.

entries.title: Tools and Choices
entries.text: Some keepers enjoy placing every light themselves. Others prefer to describe a plan and watch it unfold. The craft belongs to both. Automation preserves a decision; it does not supply its purpose.

entries.title: The Fifth Rebuilding
entries.text: By the fifth rebuilding, the keeper stopped counting lost hulls and started noticing familiar routes. Learning had become visible in the speed of the harbor’s return.

entries.title: A Margin for Doubt
entries.text: The best charts leave room for notes. Forecasts carry assumptions; plans meet weather. A keeper who writes down uncertainty gives the next watch something more useful than confidence alone.

entries.title: Six Safe Passages
entries.text: No two of the six passages ask for exactly the same fleet. That difference is the final lesson of the restoration. A collection of answers can be stronger than a single rule.

entries.title: The Last Dark Window
entries.text: The last window lit was an ordinary workshop facing away from the sea. Its owner said the horizon mattered more. The keepers lit it anyway. Returning home is part of a voyage.

entries.title: Beyond the Dawn
entries.text: When the restoration ended, the harbor held a quiet celebration. There were still patterns to discover and rooms to decorate. For the first time, none of them had to be finished before the lights could rest.
